subject: java
summary: Explains how to read Java source file structure including packages, imports, class definitions, and the difference between primitive and reference types.
key_points: Java source files consist of package declaration, imports, and class definition.
Primitive types store values directly; reference types store object addresses.
Method signatures reveal access level, return type, name, and parameters.
misconceptions: Using == to compare String values works the same as equals.
Package structure has no relation to directory structure.
Import statements are not important for understanding code dependencies.
check_questions: What are the three main sections of a Java source file?
When should you use equals instead of == in Java?
What information can you extract from a method signature?

fact_candidates: Components of a Java source file
Difference between primitive and reference types
scenario_candidates: Reading a class to identify its dependencies and role
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Assuming == compares content for reference types
Ignoring access modifiers when tracing method calls
